card.stem: The external wall of a dwelling house is a 400 mm concrete block wall with a full-fill insulated cavity. The wall is plastered on both sides. A triple glazed timber casement window is fixed in the external wall, as shown. The fixed frame of the window is 150 mm × 80 mm.
card.questionText: To a scale of 1:5, draw a vertical section through the top portion of the window. Show the wall, the concrete lintels and the fixed frame of the window. On your drawing, show the typical construction details from a level 300 mm below to a level 400 mm above the concrete lintels. Include four typical dimensions.

rows.verbatim: Any 7 of the above details (5 marks each)
rows.contextNote: Credit the best SEVEN acceptable details at 5 marks each, capped at 35. Marked details: 19 mm external plaster; 100 mm block outer leaf; 200 mm thermal insulation; stepped DPC/cavity tie; 100 mm block inner leaf; 15 mm internal plaster; prestressed concrete lintels 100 × 70 mm; window head 150 × 80 mm; triple glazing with low-e glass.
Four appropriate typical dimensions on the section.

card.stem: A young couple have bought an old, uninsulated house. They wish to improve the insulation properties of the house and have decided to start by insulating the attic space. The sketch shows the ceiling joists and the trapdoor to the attic. The ceiling joists are 200 mm × 40 mm.
card.questionText: Draw a large freehand sketch of the triangular attic space. On your sketch show the typical design detailing necessary to highly insulate the attic at ceiling joist level. Recommend a preferred insulation type and give its typical thickness.

card.stem: The sketch shows a reinforced concrete strip foundation, and a 400 mm cavity wall for a new house.
card.questionText: Using notes and freehand sketches show the typical construction details of the strip foundation supporting the concrete block wall. Indicate the position of the wall on the foundation and the location of the steel reinforcement in the foundation. Include three typical dimensions in your sketch.

rows.contextNote: A sketch of the reinforced strip foundation under the cavity wall, such as 1100 × 350 mm.

rows.verbatim: Position of walls on strip foundation
rows.contextNote: The wall centred on the foundation, with equal projections on both sides.

card.questionText: Explain, with the aid of notes and freehand sketches, any five of the following: carbon monoxide alarm; grab rail; furniture castor; laminated safety glass; eaves gutter; balusters; sapwood; bridle joint; fluorescent lighting.

rows.contextNote: Explain any five of the nine terms. Each term is marked separately: primary communication of relevant information 6 and other communication 4, in notes or sketches (the scheme reserves no fixed split between them). Carbon monoxide alarm: detects carbon monoxide and sounds an alarm before dangerous levels build up in a room, preventing poisoning by a colourless, tasteless, odourless "silent killer". Grab rail: a safety rail, usually stainless steel, chromed or plastic-coated metal, giving support and balance, lessening fatigue and something to grip in a slip or fall. Furniture castor: a wheel with a fixing plate or screw, fitted to tables, chairs and desks for easy movement; made of cast iron, plastic, nylon, steel or aluminium. Laminated safety glass: glass that holds together when shattered, held by a polyvinyl butyral (PVB) or ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA) interlayer between the sheets. Eaves gutter: fixed to the fascia, it collects rainwater from pitched or flat roofs and discharges it to an outlet or downpipe; cast iron, uPVC, aluminium, galvanised steel, copper or zinc. Balusters: vertical hardwood or softwood members between the string and the handrail, supporting the handrail; generally 38 × 38 or 44 × 44 mm, square or turned, no more than 100 mm apart. Sapwood: the outer, newer wood of a tree’s cross section, carrying the sap; lighter in colour, softer and less durable than heartwood. Bridle joint: a strong woodworking joint, tee or corner, used in furniture and frame construction, such as joining table rails to uprights. Fluorescent lighting: a low-pressure mercury-vapour discharge lamp whose ultraviolet light makes a phosphor coating glow; dearer to buy but cheaper to run; used in workplaces and homes.
